questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to be polite to colleagues at work
Ways of apologising, especially in public
Why British people are often rude to tourists
How politicians win elections by saying sorry
questions.why: Beth says they'll discuss ways of saying sorry, and they look at research on public apologies.

questions.q: What does Neil mean if he says “Oh, I'm sorry” after you tell him you're ill?
options: That it was his fault
That he doesn't believe you
That he feels sympathy for you
That he isn't really sorry
questions.why: He says it means: I sympathise, and I hope you get better soon.

questions.q: What does Beth say about the British?
options: They are world champions at apologising
They rarely say sorry
They only apologise at work
They find apologising embarrassing
questions.why: Beth says 'the British are world champions at apologising'.

questions.q: Where did Professor Louise Mullany do much of her research?
options: In schools, colleges and universities
In shops, cafés and restaurants
In families at home with children
At work, in the media and politics
questions.why: She did research in the workplace, in the media and on politicians in particular.

questions.q: According to Professor Mullany, what happens if public figures don't apologise?
options: It is seen as a big social mistake
Nobody notices
They have to pay a fine
They become more popular
questions.why: She says if they don't apologise, 'that's a big faux pas'.

questions.q: Why does Neil think politicians hate apologising?
options: They are always far too busy to do it
It means taking responsibility sincerely
Their advisers always tell them not to
It could cost them a lot of money in court
questions.why: He says saying sorry means taking responsibility, and the apology needs to be sincere.

questions.q: What was unusual about Boris Johnson's apology, according to Professor Mullany?
options: He refused to apologise at all, even when asked
He apologised only once, in a written letter
He blamed other politicians completely for it
He took responsibility but said he didn't know
questions.why: She says he said 'I am responsible', but with the caveat he wasn't certain he was breaking the rules.

questions.q: Did Boris Johnson manage to move on from the 'Partygate' scandal?
options: Yes, as soon as he paid the fine
Yes, because people accepted his humility
No, because many people didn't trust him
No, because he never apologised
questions.why: Beth says many people didn't trust him and he couldn't draw a line under the scandal.
